label: Pixel
feel: 2D pixel art with hard square texels, 16 a metre, whole screen pixels a texel, at most 32 colours a picture, a one-texel outline in each thing's own deep shade. For example a cosy town seen from above in three-quarter view (villagers with their own skin, hair and clothes, soft paths and pond shores, houses and trees to walk behind), or a cave seen from the side; what the place is, is the game's.

alternates.why: the same hard pixels on a deep blue night

three.notes: a tile map (gf-tilemap-1): top-down field or side-on stage. Seen from above a kind may have soft edges (a path, a pond, a field: "edges": "blend"), join itself (a fence, a wall, a hedge: "connect"), carry dressing (flowers and tufts in the grass, crops in the soil: "dress") or be a set piece (a house, a tree: "piece"); runtimes/three/worlds/pixel-town.json is a whole town to copy

godot.notes: side-on stages and fields seen from above (gf-tilemap-1 read from slots); this kind's Godot look is side-on, so a field keeps the runtime's own background

bodies.notes: Villagers drawn by the kit (runtimes/three/tools/pixel/folk.mjs, a layered paper doll): twelve people and the player, five skin tones. gf-flat-1: 6 frames, 3 rows from above (down, side, up; side mirrored is the fourth facing) and 1 row side-on, 32 px cells; every sheet passes the flat judge. The player's light grey shirt takes the seat colour; other roles get a villager by their words.

audio.character: chiptune: square-wave blips, coins and jumps straight from the synth presets, nothing pitched down

mechanics.why: collecting, a tile board, a shop and a level at a time. Suggestions only.
